items.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Duo Arrives in Stores: Smartphone Review
items.author: Brian X. Chen and Camille Cohen
items.content: <article>The first-generation Apple foldable may feel awkward, but it’s an intriguing step toward merging phones and tablets into one.</article>

items.title: Why Anger About Data Centers and Energy Prices May Not Swing Votes
items.author: Rebecca F. Elliott and Maddie McGarvey
items.content: <article>In Ohio, many voters say their frustration about the increase in electricity and fuel prices and the growth of data centers won’t influence whom they vote for.</article>

items.title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
items.author: Karla Adam and Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.</article>

items.title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
items.author: Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.</article>

items.title: PHP Security Flaw Sets Off Global Rush to Patch, Leaving Websites Offline
items.author: Lynsey Chutel, Amelia Nierenberg and Brian O. Otieno
items.content: <article>Governments and businesses around the world scrambled to prevent hackers from exploiting a vulnerability in PHP, a popular programming language.</article>

items.title: How the A.I. Boom Is Driving Up Sales of Gray Paint
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>Tech companies are painting data centers with gray coatings on top of gray concrete and steel to resist fire, rust and static electricity. That has made data centers a fast-growing market for paint makers.</article>

items.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
items.author: Eli Tan and Theodore Schleifer
items.content: <article>The billionaire told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.</article>

items.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion Over Cambridge Analytica Privacy Violations
items.author: Eli Tan and Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>The penalty, one of the largest levied against a tech giant, stemmed from a lawsuit by New Mexico claiming the social media company had misled users about their data privacy.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands.</article>

items.title: Meta Earnings Show Increased A.I. Spending, Even as Cash Pressures Grow
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>The spending has hurt the Silicon Valley giant’s cash flow, which turned negative. Meta said it would issue a new class of stock to help it raise more money.</article>

items.title: A.I. Discovered a Critical Vulnerability in PHP, a Coding Language Behind Many Websites
items.author: Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>The disclosure heightened concerns about A.I.’s potential to upend cybersecurity unless shortcomings are addressed.</article>

items.title: GM Aims to Bring ‘Eyes-Off’ Driving to AI-Powered Cars Within 2 Years

items.content: <article>General Motors is seeking help from artificial intelligence to keep up with Chinese companies that introduce vehicles very quickly.</article>

items.title: How The New York Times Reports on A.I. Images

items.content: <article>A Times reporter and editors discuss the challenges of sifting through what’s real and what’s not in pursuit of the news.</article>

items.title: UK to Headphone Dodgers on Trains: Shush
items.author: Megan Specia
items.content: <article>Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a campaign against listening to music or videos without headphones on public transportation. We asked London commuters to weigh in.</article>

items.title: China Criticizes U.S. Ban on DeepSeek A.I. in Government Systems
items.author: Ephrat Livni
items.content: <article>The response came after Homeland Security ordered the removal and exclusion of products developed by the Chinese company.</article>

items.title: Netflix Is Great at Making Money. Its Problem Is Keeping Viewers Hooked.
items.author: Nicole Sperling
items.content: <article>The streaming service reported a 12 percent increase in quarterly revenue, but acknowledged that stagnant viewership, particularly in the U.S. and Canada, was a major concern.</article>

items.title: SpaceX Swings to a Profit, as A.I. Business Grows
items.author: Ryan Mac and Kate Conger
items.content: <article>Elon Musk’s rocket company said its artificial intelligence spending had soared, but revenue more than doubled from its Starlink internet satellite service and A.I. products.</article>

items.title: Boeing’s Large 737 Max Jet Secures U.S. Approval
items.author: Niraj Chokshi
items.content: <article>After years of delay, the Federal Aviation Administration certified the 737 Max 10, the largest version of Boeing’s most popular plane.</article>

items.title: Joel Kaplan, Meta’s Global Policy Chief, to Leave After 15 Years
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Joel Kaplan, a former adviser to George W. Bush known for his Republican ties, had helped Meta build its relationship with the Trump administration.</article>

items.title: Google Reports Cloud Disruptions in Europe
items.author: Leo Sands
items.content: <article>The disruptions began around 7 a.m. in London after what the tech giant called a “power event.”</article>

items.title: Saudis Aided Family of Engineer Accused of Bugging OpenAI, Prosecutors Say
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>Saudi officials paid for his wife and son to fly out of the U.S. and offered to cover his bail, according to court filings. A judge ordered the engineer to remain in custody.</article>

items.title: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
items.author: Ryan Mac
items.content: <article>Anthropic, an A.I. rival to SpaceX, earlier said it would form a “public benefit fund” and other tech moguls have contributed to savings accounts for children.</article>
